text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help determine the cause of your infant's bilious vomiting and abdominal distension, could you tell me exactly how old the baby is and if they have had any bowel movements since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Since the infant has not passed meconium within the first 48 hours of life, I would like to examine his rectal area; does he appear to have a normal anal opening, and did you notice any explosive stool release when you changed his diaper recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Inability to pass meconium, Abdominal distension.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of delayed meconium passage, bilious vomiting, and abdominal distension in a newborn strongly suggest Hirschsprung disease or meconium ileus. I will request an abdominal X-ray and an urgent rectal biopsy to differentiate between these conditions. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray; REQUEST TEST: Rectal_Biopsy
